name: combobox
description: Filterable single-select with an animated custom listbox, built on the dropdown open/close machine

meta.name: Combobox
meta.description: Filterable single-select with an animated custom listbox, built on the dropdown open/close machine

props.name: id
props.description: Base id for the input and its listbox/aria wiring; auto-generated when omitted.

props.name: options
props.description: The selectable options.

props.name: value
props.description: The controlled value.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initial value when uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the selected option value (or undefined when cleared).

props.name: clearable
props.description: When true, shows a control to clear the selected value.

props.name: searchable
props.description: When true the field is a text input that filters the list as the user types (the APG editable combobox). When false it is a button that opens the list, and type-to-select jumps to a matching option (the APG select-only combobox).

props.name: loading
props.description: When true, the list reports itself as busy and shows a loading row instead of the empty message.

props.name: onSearchChange
props.description: Called with the search text on every keystroke. Pair it with filter={() => true} for a server-driven list.

props.name: filter
props.description: Replaces the built-in diacritic-insensitive matcher.

props.name: creatable
props.description: When true, offers the current search text as a new option.

props.name: onCreate
props.description: Called with the typed label when the user picks the "create" row.

props.name: name
props.description: Submitted with a surrounding form — a hidden input carrying the selected value.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the control as required for assistive technology.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state of the listbox.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: The initial open state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the listbox opens or closes.

props.name: label
props.description: Text label for the control.

props.name: hint
props.description: Supplementary hint text shown with the control.

props.name: error
props.description: Error message shown when the value is invalid.

props.name: size
props.description: Visual size of the component (e.g. 'sm', 'md', 'lg').

props.name: disabled
props.description: When true, disables the control and removes it from the tab order.

props.name: labels
props.description: Overrides for the component’s user-visible strings (i18n).

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS class names merged onto the root element.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Wired automatically by a wrapping `Field` — its label id, forwarded to the focusable control so the Field's label names it.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: Wired automatically by a wrapping `Field` — the ids of its hint/error text, forwarded to the focusable control so the supporting text is announced.

props.name: aria-invalid
props.description: Wired automatically by a wrapping `Field` when it is in an error state.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Invisible accessible name, for when a visible element outside this component already labels it and `label` would render that text a second time. ⚠ `label` on this component is **visible**; `IconButton.label`/`Sparkline.label` are invisible names, which is the prior that costs adopters a duplicated label. The raw DOM `aria-label` still wins over this.

examples.title: Grouped options
examples.description: Options carrying a group render under a labelled role="group" heading.

examples.title: Remote search
examples.description: filter={() => true} hands filtering to the server; loading marks the list busy between keystroke and response.

examples.title: Select-only
examples.description: A button rather than a text field; printable characters type-to-select, and Home/End jump the list.

examples.title: Basic combobox
examples.code:
<Combobox
  label="Country"
  options={[
    { value: 'us', label: 'United States' },
    { value: 'de', label: 'Germany' },
    { value: 'fr', label: 'France' },
  ]}
  onValueChange={(value) => console.log(value)}
/>

whenToUse: Single-select from a long list where type-to-filter makes finding an option faster
Form fields where the value is one of many known options (country, assignee, repository)
whenNotToUse: Short option lists (≈2–7) where filtering adds no value — use Select or SegmentedControl
Triggering actions or commands — use Dropdown or CommandMenu

antiPatterns.bad: Using Combobox to fire actions like "Delete" or "Export"
antiPatterns.good: Use Dropdown for actions; Combobox is for picking a value
antiPatterns.why: Combobox has role="combobox" with a listbox of selectable values and onValueChange semantics — actions belong in a menu

antiPatterns.good: Keep the default searchable so the user can filter
antiPatterns.why: Type-to-select still jumps to a matching option, but without a visible filter a 200-row list is an unusable scroll; searchable={false} is for short lists
The built-in matcher still runs over the server’s results and filters them a second time against the same query, hiding rows the server deliberately returned

related.name: Select
related.reason: Use for short lists that do not need type-to-filter

related.name: MultiSelect
related.reason: Use when more than one value can be selected

related.name: CommandMenu
related.reason: Use the Cmd+K palette for command/navigation search rather than value selection

intent.a11yRationale: Two APG combobox shapes, chosen by `searchable`. With searchable (the default) the field is an <input role="combobox"> with aria-autocomplete="list" that filters as the user types — the APG editable combobox. With searchable={false} it is a <button role="combobox"> and printable characters type-to-select — the APG select-only combobox. Either way the field itself keeps DOM focus and owns aria-expanded, aria-controls and aria-activedescendant, so assistive technology tracks the active option as the arrows move it; the previous build put aria-activedescendant on a trigger while focus had moved into a separate search input, so nothing was tracked. The listbox holds only role="option" rows (with aria-selected and aria-disabled) and role="group" headings — the loading and no-results messages are siblings of it, as role="listbox" owns no other children. ArrowUp/ArrowDown skip disabled rows and wrap, PageUp/PageDown move by ten, Alt+ArrowDown opens without moving the active option and Alt+ArrowUp closes keeping the value, Enter selects, Escape closes and returns focus to the field, and Tab closes without stealing focus back. Home/End jump the list only in the select-only variant, because in the editable one they belong to the text caret. Outside-pointer and Escape dismissal come from the shared DismissableLayer rather than a hand-rolled document listener. A polite live region reports the result count as the filter narrows. Selection, the active row and the focus ring each carry a non-colour channel under forced-colors, and every control reaches the coarse-pointer target minimum.

flexibility.note: Filtering can be toggled off for short lists via searchable={false}
Listbox/field styling resolves to semantic --cascivo-color-* / --cascivo-radius-* tokens
